paragraphs.text: This was both an argument of the truth of his humanity (that he was thronged and thrust together by the unmannerly multitude) and a part of his passion.
paragraphs.anchor: As the people pressed upon him

paragraphs.text: Though they laboured last night, and had taken nothing. Ferendum et sperandum. Hope beguiles calamity, as good company doth the way.
Gr. He gently asked him, ηρωτησεν, will you be pleased to thrust out a little? See Php 2:8-9. Posse el nolle, nobile est.
Any place served him for a pulpit. So if men be desirous to hear, they will make a mat a seat, a pair of legs a seat.
paragraphs.anchor: Taught the people out of the ship

paragraphs.text: This is the fare he pays them, for the use of their ship. No man loseth by Christ.
Omnia feci, et nihil expedit, said Severus the emperor. (Spartian.) See Heb 2:13; Hag 2:6. if God stop not that hole in the bottom of the bag, all will run through.
If ministers be put so to complain, it is to be feared that Satan caught the fish ere they came to their net.
Yet the fishes got not out, which some note for another miracle.
Here the dumb fishes do clearly preach Christ to be the Son of God.
Gr. A man a sinner, ανηρ αμαρτωλος, a very mixture and compound of dirt and sin. See the like phrase, Num 32:14.
paragraphs.anchor: For I am a sinful man

paragraphs.text: Gr. Fear seized upon him, and surrounded him, περιεσχεν, as Tacitus saith, Induere pavores.

They had given their names to him before, Joh 1:43; but now they see by this miracle his power to provide for them, they leave all to live with him. We love to see how we shall subsist.
paragraphs.anchor: They forsook all, and followed him

paragraphs.text: It is a ready way to speed, to found our prayers upon the power of God.
So ready is Christ to gratify his suppliants, yea, to be commanded by them, Isa 45:11.
For a Bill of Indictment against them. Reprobates shall give a heavy account to God of all the means and offers of grace.
Fame follows them that comes from it, and the contrary: as the crocodile doth.
Pray, if you mean to prosper.
So it is, when any ordinance is afoot.

Epulum splendidum, a sumptuous feast; so St Luke’s word δοχην here signifieth. But when St Matthew himself speaks of it, he saith only that Christ came home and ate bread with him: to teach us, saith one, that another man’s mouth should praise us, and not our own, Pro 27:2. {See Trapp on "Pro 27:2"}
